question: What specific named datasets or benchmarks were used to evaluate or test this AI model?
keywords: evaluation benchmark test dataset tested evaluated assessment validation
description: Per SPDX 3.0.1 testedOn relationship: identifies the specific datasets or benchmarks used to evaluate the AI model. Examples include GLUE, SuperGLUE, MMLU, HellaSwag, etc. Maps to SPDX testedOn relationship and CycloneDX modelCard.datasets with type=evaluation.

retrieval.hypothetical_passage:
## Evaluation

We evaluate on the GLUE and SuperGLUE benchmarks, MMLU (5-shot), HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, and TruthfulQA. For multilingual capability we report XNLI and FLORES-200. Code generation is measured on HumanEval and MBPP. Results are reported as accuracy or pass@1 against the held-out test split of each benchmark; we did not tune hyperparameters on the evaluation sets.

extraction.instruction: Extract the named datasets or benchmarks used to EVALUATE/TEST this AI model. Return only the canonical dataset names, comma-separated. CRITICAL: do NOT include the model's training corpus — those belong in trainedOnDatasets, not here.
extraction.field_spec: AIkaBoOM-internal. Value space: a list of dataset/benchmark names (canonical short forms preferred, e.g. `GLUE`, `MMLU`, `HumanEval`). Maps to SPDX `testedOn` relationship and CycloneDX `modelCard.datasets` with `type=evaluation`.
extraction.output_guidance:
INCLUDE a dataset only if the source presents it as something the model was MEASURED on. Look for verbs like: 'evaluated on', 'tested on', 'benchmark', 'we report results on', 'measured on', 'zero-shot/few-shot accuracy on', 'pass@1 on'. Section markers that signal evaluation: 'Evaluation', 'Results', 'Benchmarks', 'Experiments', 'Test', or results tables with numeric scores per dataset.

EXCLUDE any dataset that only appears in: 'Training Data', 'Pretraining Corpus', 'Fine-tuning', 'training mixture', 'we trained on …', 'pre-trained on …'. A web-scale corpus the model was trained on (BookCorpus, Wikipedia, Common Crawl, C4, The Pile, OpenWebText, YFCC100M, LAION, web-scraped image-text pairs) is NOT an evaluation dataset.

WORKED EXAMPLES:
• BERT paper says 'pre-trained on BookCorpus and Wikipedia' AND reports GLUE/SQuAD scores → testedOn = `GLUE, SQuAD` (NOT BookCorpus, NOT Wikipedia).
• CLIP paper trains on 400M (image,text) web pairs and reports zero-shot accuracy on 30+ benchmarks (Food101, CIFAR10, …, ImageNet) → testedOn lists those 30+ benchmarks. The 400M web pairs go in trainedOnDatasets, not here.
• If a dataset name appears in BOTH a training section AND a results table (rare — e.g. paper says 'we fine-tuned on SQuAD and report F1 on SQuAD'), include it in BOTH testedOn AND trainedOn lists.
• If the only data discussed is the training corpus and no evaluation/benchmark is mentioned, return noAssertion.

Return concrete dataset names only; preserve official capitalization (`SQuAD`, `HellaSwag`, `HumanEval`). De-duplicate across sections. If evaluation is mentioned but no specific dataset is named (e.g. 'an internal test set'), or if evaluation is not discussed at all, return noAssertion.
